function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t something that was “discovered” by a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been known and studied for millennia. Here’s a quick overview of some key figures who helped turn observations of static charge and lightning into the science of electricity we know today:

| Time period | Person | Contribution |
|-------------|--------|--------------|
| **c. 600 BC** | **Thales of Miletus** | First recorded observation of static electricity by rubbing amber (Greek *elektron*). |
| **c. 400 BC** | **Pythagoras** | Noted that rubbing amber produced an attraction between objects. |
| **c. 300 BC** | **Aristotle** | Discussed the properties of static charge. |
| **c. 1600** | **William Gilbert** | Published *De Magnete*, coined the term *electricus* for amber, distinguished magnetism from static electricity. |
| **c. 1650** | **Robert Boyle** | Conducted experiments on static electricity and coined the term *electrical*. |
| **c. 1700** | **Otto von Guericke** | Demonstrated the effect of static charge on air. |
| **c. 1752** | **Benjamin Franklin** | Conducted the famous kite experiment, showing that lightning is electrical. Introduced the concepts of positive and negative charge. |
| **c. 1800** | **Alessandro Volta** | Invented the voltaic pile (the first battery), proving that electricity can be generated chemically. |
| **c. 1801** | **Hans Christian Ørsted** | Discovered the relationship between electricity and magnetism (electromagnetism). |
| **c. 1807** | **Michael Faraday** | Developed the principles of electromagnetic induction. |
| **c. 1820** | **André-Marie Ampère** | Formulated Ampère’s law, describing the magnetic field produced by electric currents. |
| **c. 1831** | **James Clerk Maxwell** | Unified electricity and magnetism into Maxwell’s equations. |

So while no single individual “discovered” electricity, the cumulative work of these and many other scientists over centuries turned ancient observations into the modern field of electromagnetism.
